subject: polity
core_concepts: Integrated yet independent single judiciary with High Courts heading State judicial administration under Part VI, Chapter V (Articles 214-231).
Article 214 mandates a High Court for each State, subject to Parliament establishing common High Courts under Article 231.
High Court as a Court of Record (Article 215) with perpetual memory, evidentiary value, and summary power to punish for its own contempt and contempt of subordinate courts.
Flexible Court Strength (Article 216) determined from time to time by the President of India (not fixed by Parliament).
Appointment of Judges (Article 217) by President under warrant under hand and seal after consultation with CJI, Governor, and Chief Justice of HC (and Collegium recommendations).
Writ Jurisdiction (Article 226) for Fundamental Rights and any other legal purpose; broader than Supreme Court under Article 32, but discretionary.
Superintendence Power (Article 227) over all courts and tribunals (administrative + judicial), strictly excluding Armed Forces / military tribunals.
Administrative independence (Article 229): CJ of High Court appoints officers/staff and determines conditions of service.

constitutional_articles.Article 216: Constitution of High Courts (Strength determined by President)

constitutional_articles.Article 220: Restriction on practice after being a permanent Judge (only in SC and other HCs)

constitutional_articles.Article 223: Appointment of acting Chief Justice by President
constitutional_articles.Article 224: Appointment of additional (max 2 years) and acting Judges by President

historical_and_institutional_facts.Indian High Courts Act 1861: Authorized British Crown to establish High Courts replacing Supreme Courts and Sadar Adalats.
historical_and_institutional_facts.1862 Establishments: Calcutta (July 1, 1862), Bombay (August 14, 1862), Madras (August 15, 1862). Calcutta is the oldest HC.
historical_and_institutional_facts.Fourth High Court: Allahabad High Court (established at Agra in 1866 as HC of Judicature for NW Provinces, shifted to Allahabad in 1869).
historical_and_institutional_facts.Newest High Courts (2019): Andhra Pradesh High Court (Amaravati) and Telangana High Court (Hyderabad), established Jan 1, 2019.
historical_and_institutional_facts.UTs with own High Courts: NCT of Delhi (Delhi HC, 1966) and Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh (common HC for the two UTs).

Common High Courts.Bombay HC: Maharashtra, Goa, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu (Benches: Nagpur, Panaji, Aurangabad).
Common High Courts.Guwahati HC: Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh (Benches: Kohima, Aizawl, Itanagar).
Common High Courts.Calcutta HC: West Bengal, Andaman and Nicobar Islands (Circuit Bench: Port Blair; Jalpaiguri).
Common High Courts.Madras HC: Tamil Nadu, Puducherry (Permanent Bench at Madurai, 2004).

qualifications_and_tenure.citizenship: Must be a citizen of India.
qualifications_and_tenure.judicial_office: Held a judicial office in the territory of India for at least 10 years, OR
qualifications_and_tenure.advocate_experience: Advocate of a High Court (or two or more such courts in succession) for at least 10 years.
qualifications_and_tenure.distinguished_jurist: NO provision for distinguished jurist in High Courts (unlike Supreme Court Article 124(3)(c)).
qualifications_and_tenure.minimum_age: No minimum age prescribed in the Constitution.
qualifications_and_tenure.retirement_age: 62 years (raised from 60 to 62 by the 15th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1963).
qualifications_and_tenure.resignation: In writing addressed to the PRESIDENT of India (NOT Governor).
qualifications_and_tenure.removal: By President on parliamentary address supported by special majority under Judges Enquiry Act 1968 on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
qualifications_and_tenure.oath: Administered by GOVERNOR of the State or person appointed by him (Schedule III).

financial_provisions.salaries_and_allowances: Charged upon Consolidated Fund of the STATE (cannot be varied to disadvantage except during Financial Emergency under Art 360).
financial_provisions.pension: Charged upon Consolidated Fund of INDIA (Article 112(3)(d)(iii)). State legislature cannot vote on pension!

tnpsc_traps: Trap 1: Governor Appointment Fallacy - HC Judges appointed by PRESIDENT, not Governor.
Trap 2: Retirement Age Swap - 62 years for HC (15th Amendment 1963), not 65 years (SC).
Trap 3: Distinguished Jurist Exclusion - Does NOT apply to High Courts; exists ONLY for Supreme Court.
Trap 4: Resignation Recipient - Addressed to PRESIDENT, not Governor.
Trap 5: Salary vs Pension Charge - Salary charged on State Consolidated Fund; Pension charged on Consolidated Fund of India.
Trap 6: Writ Jurisdiction Scope - HC (Art 226) is wider than SC (Art 32) because HC issues writs for FRs and other legal rights; but Art 226 is discretionary while Art 32 is a guaranteed FR.
Trap 7: Art 227 Superintendence - Administrative and judicial, but EXCLUDES military courts and tribunals (courts martial).
Trap 8: Death Sentence Confirmation - Sessions court capital sentence cannot be executed without High Court confirmation, even if accused does not appeal.
Trap 9: Subordinate Judiciary Division of Power - District Judges appointed by Governor (Art 233); postings, promotions, and discipline controlled by High Court (Art 235).
Trap 10: Common HC Establishment - Established by PARLIAMENT by law (Art 231), not by President or Governor.
